## 🎧 Choose your next record {color="purple"}
Start with **45 Grave → Kommunity FK → Cinema Strange**. Two close-match experiments and one theatrical contrast, with prior listening unknown.
<database url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af4815c97bbf87eaa2c7c9a" inline="true" data-source-url="collection://dba7ad92-df45-4403-8caa-97e61a04e491"></database>
<details>
<summary>How to use the gallery</summary>
	**Next listens:** your current three-record route.
	**Your stated favorites:** Pornography and Disintegration, which you explicitly named.
	**Deathrock:** the current route plus the Christian Death historical reference.
	**Atmospheric detours:** Lycia’s Cold, retained from the earlier mixed batch.
	**All albums:** all eleven dossiers, including the original onboarding references and earlier optional recommendations.
	“Unknown” means session/edition details have not been supplied. It does not mean a favorite album is unheard. Each dossier distinguishes sourced facts, edition notes, and editorial listening questions.
</details>
---
## 🖤 Your listening compass {color="purple"}
<columns>
	<column ratio="33">
		<callout icon="🌑" color="purple_bg">
			**Sinister atmosphere**
			You favor darkness and a strong sense of mood. Name the sound that creates it.
		</callout>
		<callout icon="🔊" color="gray_bg">
			**Guitar & bass weight**
			You like heavy, loud sounds. Compare attack, bass presence, and sustained texture.
		</callout>
	</column>
	<column ratio="34">
		<callout icon="🥁" color="purple_bg">
			**Rhythmic grip**
			You favor catchy rhythms. Follow the pulse and identify the repeating figure.
		</callout>
		<callout icon="🪝" color="gray_bg">
			**Memorable hooks**
			A listening hypothesis from your catchy-rhythm preference: name the moment that stays with you.
		</callout>
	</column>
	<column ratio="33">
		<callout icon="🦇" color="purple_bg">
			**Distinctive character**
			You like unique sonic identities. Describe what separates a recording from familiar references.
		</callout>
		<callout icon="🎭" color="gray_bg">
			**Current route: raw deathrock**
			Compare attack, rough texture, and theatrical voice without assuming every record supplies all three.
		</callout>
	</column>
</columns>
**Confirmed album likes:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af481d29c75e22feb50b6ae"/> and <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af481d38d75e7613eef52b3"/>.
**Still to clarify:** the exact Sisters of Mercy “first two records,” “Asmodi Bizarre,” “osferatu,” and “Pale descent.” Your original wording and full unranked artist list remain in <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af481959551fa712f5cabc7">Original research & preference archive — 9 October 2026</mention-page>.
<details>
<summary>Compare a sample in one minute</summary>
	1. **Hook:** what musical gesture do you remember?
	2. **Texture:** where does the weight or atmosphere come from?
	3. **Reaction:** what draws you in, and what reduces your interest?
	Report the edition and whether you sampled tracks or heard the full album. Leave a score blank unless you choose to give one.
</details>
<details>
<summary>Six sound cues</summary>
	### Rhythm and grip
	Follow the pulse, then the bass line. Catchiness might come from a recurring bass figure, a drum accent, or the vocal phrasing. Name the element holding your attention.
	### Attack and weight
	Attack is the initial strike of a note or drum hit. Weight concerns the impression of depth and force. Loud playback, strong bass, distorted guitars, and hard drumming do not always produce the same effect.
	### Guitar texture
	Distinguish sharp rhythmic strokes, ringing melodic lines, abrasive noise, and sustained layers. A heavily effected guitar does not automatically mean a heavier song.
	### Space and atmosphere
	Reverb gives a sense of space and decay. Delay adds repeated echoes. Listen for the balance between close, immediate sounds and distant layers.
	### Voice and character
	Notice register, urgency, theatrical phrasing, and restraint. Sinister atmosphere might come from delivery rather than lyrics or low pitch alone.
	### Hooks and identity
	Identify the moment you remember after the track ends. Then ask what separates the band from others you enjoy: rhythm, tone, melody, arrangement, or vocal character.
</details>
---
## 📝 Keep the reaction, find the next record {color="purple"}
Use **Quick entry** to record a real session, or add a row in **Listening sessions**. Link the album, distinguish sample/full listen, and preserve your exact feedback. Listening date and reported date are separate; leave unknown details blank.
<database url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af48125a79ae83612c4bd2e" inline="true" data-source-url="collection://ab0f13a4-97c5-4997-be8b-1bb36f8a8598"></database>
<callout icon="📝" color="gray_bg">
	**Your journal is ready and empty.**
	Select **Listen again** or **Find more like this** when those actions match your reaction; their filtered views become your follow-up lists. The optional score has no imposed scale.
</callout>
---
## 🕯️ Follow the history {color="purple"}
A selective path through recording references, club context, and a Chilean discovery lead, **1980–2024**. Open a milestone for its evidence and next listening question.
<database url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af481cd9b50f214123cca19" inline="true" data-source-url="collection://ba628b08-160d-4a58-8176-72c4ad26df62"></database>
<details>
<summary>Reading dates and gaps</summary>
	The timeline bars span calendar years for visual placement. January 1 and December 31 are display boundaries, not asserted release dates. The Batcave bar follows the retrospective’s 1982–1985 coverage rather than a verified opening-to-closure interval.
	Use **Chronological index** for a compact year-sorted view. This is a listening-oriented history, not an exhaustive account: early precursors, wider regional scenes, and much of the intervening decades remain research tasks.
</details>
---
## 🗺️ Explore the scene atlas {color="purple"}
Five entry points connect recordings with local context: **Los Angeles, London, German revival networks, Chile, and an Arizona atmospheric detour**. Cards distinguish source-backed overviews from research leads.
<database url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4e10956af481e1abaeda54da1fedc5" inline="true" data-source-url="collection://2b8010e3-1a71-44a8-9b41-4845f97edd8f"></database>
<details>
<summary>A scene is a listening question</summary>
	**Los Angeles:** compare attack, guitar texture, and vocal character across three early records.
	**London:** explore club culture and theatrical performance; Batcave is also a scene reference.
	**Germany:** follow labels, festivals, and circulation without assigning one national sound.
	**Chile:** build from a documented Puerto Montt lead toward wider local research.
	**Arizona:** use Lycia as a related atmospheric comparison, not a complete regional history.
	Open **Research gaps** for the less-developed paths. Historic venue and festival references are not current event recommendations.
</details>
---
## 📸 Archive wall {color="purple"}
<columns>
	<column ratio="50">
		![Dinah Cancer of 45 Grave, Long Beach, 5 October 2007. Photo: Morven.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Dinah_Cancer_45_Grave_Blue_Cafe_Long_Beach_4.jpg/1280px-Dinah_Cancer_45_Grave_Blue_Cafe_Long_Beach_4.jpg)

	</column>
	<column ratio="50">
		![The Cure performing in Rome, 2008. Photo: Moloch981.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fd/The_Cure_Live_Roma_2008_-_3.jpg)
		[Photo and credit](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Cure_Live_Roma_2008_-_3.jpg). Public domain. Original photo, no edits.
	</column>
</columns>
These later performances do not document every album’s recording lineup. Cover: Patrik Mata, identified as Wings, Los Angeles, 1984, on the [official Kommunity FK discography](https://kommunityfk.wixsite.com/kommunityfk/discography); photographer is not identified there.

	Keep **editorial recommendations**, **attributed published lists**, and **your personal favorites** separate. No annual ranking or personal scores have been completed. Core annual album eligibility remains original gothic-rock studio full-lengths; identify any deathrock/adjacent inclusion and keep other formats separate.

## Why this belongs here
Test repetition, abrasion, and distinctive identity against your Voodoo Church and Christian Death interests. The aim is to discover whether rough texture adds tension for you.
## Recording dossier
The official discography lists the 1983 vinyl and later CD/digital editions. [Band discography](https://kommunityfk.wixsite.com/kommunityfk/discography). LA Weekly places the band in the early Los Angeles deathrock context. [Scene account](https://www.laweekly.com/the-la-deathrock-starter-guide/).

Original vinyl: Independent Project, 1983. Pictured catalog: official 2006 CD reissue with bonus live material.
[Listening / catalog route](https://kommunityfk.bandcamp.com/album/vision-and-the-voice)
## Three listening doors
- **Original-album selection** — Choose a track confirmed on the original sequence; follow one repeating instrumental figure.
- **A second original-album selection** — Compare guitar texture and the amount of empty space.
- **Live bonus comparison, optional** — Label it as bonus/live material and compare performance texture separately.
## Compare with your reference shelf
Place one original-album sample after Evil by 45 Grave. Which matters more to your reaction: immediate rhythmic grip, guitar texture, or vocal character?

It did not expose a tracklist in the retrieved page. Original sequencing, personnel, and playable full-album access still need verification. Do not substitute Something Inside Me Has Died: the official discography connects it with other releases, and LA Weekly identifies Close One Sad Eye (1985).
